title: Friendsgiving Ideas 2026: Menu, Games, Decor and a Timeline
description: Friendsgiving ideas for 2026: the best date, a 3-week host timeline, a potluck sign-up that works, menu and drink math, cheap decor and 10 games for adults.
dek: A host’s plan from the sign-up sheet to the morning after.
excerpt: When to host in 2026, a potluck sign-up that prevents five pies and no rolls, a menu for every kind of cook, turkey and wine math, cheap decor and ten games for adults.

faq.a: Friendsgiving has no fixed date. Thanksgiving 2026 is Thursday, November 26, so most groups pick the weekend before: Saturday, November 21 or Sunday, November 22. The Wednesday before and the Friday after also work, but expect some guests to be traveling. If your friends scatter for the holiday, an earlier November weekend is fine.

faq.q: Who brings the turkey to Friendsgiving?
faq.a: Usually the host, because the turkey needs the oven for hours and has to come out right before dinner. Guests bring sides, desserts and drinks that arrive ready to serve. If you’d rather not roast a whole bird, a bone-in turkey breast or a slow-cooker breast feeds a smaller group with much less oven time.

faq.q: What should I bring to Friendsgiving if I can’t cook?
faq.a: Bring something the meal can’t run without: ice, sparkling water, a batch drink, good bread from a bakery, a store-bought pie with real whipped cream, or a stack of takeout containers for leftovers. You can also claim a job instead of a dish, like setting the table or staying to wash up.

faq.q: How many dishes do you need for a Friendsgiving potluck?
faq.a: For 12 people, plan on the host’s main (plus a vegetarian main if anyone needs one), two no-oven appetizers, six sides including cranberry sauce, one bread, two desserts and two drinks. Add slots for leftover containers and cleanup, and a few guests will take two. For bigger groups, add a side for every four extra guests and a dessert for every six.

faq.q: How do you host Friendsgiving on a budget?
faq.a: Make it a true potluck, cover only the main yourself, and skip anything that costs money but nobody remembers, like themed paper goods. The Farm Bureau’s 2025 survey priced a 16-pound frozen turkey at $21.50 on average. Decorate with candles, kraft paper, grocery-store flowers split into jars and leaves from a walk.
